title: Rpg Maker and Android Gaming Handhelds

posts.author: CardCaph
posts.body:
In recent times, gaming has gotten a lot more portable with things like the steam deck and other handheld devices.
One type of handheld that has recently caught my eye is android gaming handhelds. I guess a way to describe them would be a mini tablet built like a gamepad? I recently bought one myself called the Mangmi Air X (pictured).
What I found most interesting is that it actually feels nice to play on and hold. It's small, and pretty comparable to my Switch Lite.
Though right, the point
: there was talk of RPG Maker MV and MZ(?) being able to port to android, and as the name would suggest, this thing and a few others like it run on just that (and sometimes Linux). For a while, I always thought it was a lesser option given my growing distaste for on-screen controls over the years, but things have come a long way since then. I scrounged through different indie sites for games that happened to have a mobile port and found myself having a really good time with those that support controllers.
I guess it's also important to note that for the most part, yes, the main selling point for a majority of these devices is retro gaming (as they are also sometimes referred to as "Android Retro Handhelds"), though some of the beefier ones can do much more than that (
But my use case is probably niche and I feel like a lunatic every time I mention it to someone.)
If you are interested, I'd really recommend looking further into it. Anything I could say would not do them justice. Some are really *just* for retro gaming though, so check the specs beforehand, watch reviews, etc.
This site has some decent info listed too:
https://retrocatalog.com/
Extra extra note: It is probably worth looking into things such as URGE (Universal Ruby Game Engine -
https://urge.admenri.com/
) and EasyRPG for older Makers, but I haven't gotten a chance to delve deeper into either yet. URGE does seem to have the ability to make apks for XP, VX, and VX Ace games, but the documentation is either vague or tucked away somewhere, so I'm unsure how performant those even are. EasyRPG has a player app for its games, and that works well enough for now. If you know of any other android related shenanigans with the Makers, please do share.
I'm also down to test some games out on mine if you'd like (android 14).
